_notes: THE BLACK RAM'S CONTACT BURST -- what a landed blow draws on the body it
hit while the form is worn (skills.json black_ram_mode.transform.hit.vfx).
Not a house effect: it belongs to a skill's transform block, which is why
it is cut under Resources/Spells/ with a recipe rather than written
straight into Resources/Vfx/ the way slash_arc and impact_burst are
(docs/ART_PIPELINE.md 5c states that ownership rule).
DELIVERED, NOT GENERATED, as of this recipe -- the one thing that
changed from the placeholder this replaces. The placeholder's bytes and
the polar arithmetic that drew them (tools/make_contact_fx.py's
build_form_sheet/ram_frame, since removed as dead code -- nothing else
called --form-sheet) still live in git history; this sheet is
commissioned art. Source: output/black-ram-impact/black-ram-impact-
draft-v1.png, prompt in prompt.txt beside it. The brief asked for
2048x1024; what came back is 1774x887 with real, unbaked alpha -- the
same scale-down the water pack's own sheets shipped with, and the same
444/443 4x2 geometry as a result.
EXPLICIT RECTS, THE SAME NUMBERS AS prismatic_orb_water_contact.json,
because the sheet is the same shape for the same reason: 1774x887 over
4x2 does not divide, column edges 0/444/887/1331/1774, row edges
0/444/887 -- 444/443 alternating. Measured on THIS sheet, not assumed
from the water pack: every one of the 8 cells' content bboxes reaches at
least one of its own edges (f0 left+right+bottom, f1 left+right+bottom,
f2 left+right, f3 left+bottom, f4 top, f5 top+right, f6
left+right+bottom, f7 left+top). A floor-divided grid would clip a
sliver of a neighbour into four of these cells the same way it would
have on the water sheet; a boundary check confirms no two cells'
content actually touches across a seam (checked at all three column
seams, both rows -- the nearest approach is chips of f2 and the front of
f3 both reaching toward x=1331 from opposite sides without crossing it),
so the exact rects cut every cell clean with nothing amputated.
THE BRIEF ASKED FOR 'up to 70% of the cell at peak, nothing touches the
cell edge' and 'everything radiates RIGHTWARD' from a blow arriving on
the left. What was delivered runs fuller than that at every frame, not
just the peak, and the burst itself (f1-f3) reads as a roughly radial
flower -- spikes and the two horn arcs going up, down and left as well
as right -- rather than biased toward the strike direction. Only f0
reads as directional (a compact tail-and-point shape, tail trailing
left). Said here rather than smoothed over: it is still a strong, heavy
read and the exact-rects cut keeps every cell clean, but it is not the
confined, rightward-biased burst the prompt specifically asked for.
NO canvas: no scale step needs headroom (see below), so the largest
cell (444x444) stays the shared canvas the way an unstated one always
has.
f2 IS THE PEAK -- 'frame 3' in the prompt's own 1-based chronological
numbering (frame1 arrival, frame2 the lobe splitting, frame3 the widest
spread with the black mass still solid). Content bbox 444x411 of 444x444
(100% wide, 93% tall), touching both side edges -- measurably the
widest of the eight. NO HOLD on it, unlike the water contact's f3:
that recipe held its peak because the sequence plays at 26fps (0.038s/
frame) and the jump from the runner-up's 23% ink to the peak's 27% was
abrupt enough to read as a drawing going past rather than a blow
landing. This sheet has no fps of its own -- skills.json fits all 8
cells into 0.46s, 0.0575s/frame, already a third slower -- and the
growth into the peak is spread across three already-full frames (f0
compact, f1 already a wide flower, f2 slightly wider again) rather than
one late jump, so the peak already reads as landing rather than
flashing past. Held it would also change the frame count on disk from
8 to 9, which nothing downstream (skills.json's seconds/8 timing, the
impactX/impactY measured off f2 as cell 3 of 8) asks for.
IMPACTX/IMPACTY measured off f2, the black mass's solid core (luminance
< 60, alpha > 180, alpha-weighted centroid) rather than the whole
drawing's bbox centre, per ART_PIPELINE 5b: 0.43 across, 0.48 up from
the bottom -- close to the frame's geometric middle (0.50/0.50) but not
exactly it, and skills.json's black_ram_mode layer states both rather
than leaving the default guess to stand on a measurement this close but
not exact.
8 CELLS, ONE FOR ONE, NO sequence -- the eight cells are the eight
frames. Frame count is unchanged from the placeholder this replaces, so
no new .meta files are needed under Resources/Spells/black_ram_impact/.
keyed: false. THE ALPHA IS AUTHORED IN THE SHEET -- it is real,
delivered alpha, not luminance-keyed -- which is the one house
convention this pack still breaks, now for a different reason than the
placeholder's: ART_PIPELINE 2's luminance key exists because a glow has
no clean edge, and the most SOLID part of this sheet is still its
darkest. Keyed from luminance, the black mass would be the most
transparent thing in the frame; the source already carries a correct
cutout, confirmed by the same solid-core measurement above landing on
genuinely opaque black rather than a keyed-out haze.
